title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds automatic defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, new quantization profile templates and a unit-economics dashboard and CLI to expose per-route cost estimates and recommended profiles.
description: Summary: Provide an end-to-end autotune flow that sets safe defaults for batching and KV caching, introduces quantization profile templates for common model classes, and surfaces unit-economics recommendations in the Console and via a CLI. Motivation: Customers ship models with suboptimal batching/cache config or overly aggressive quantization and see large cost regressions or latency spikes. This PR automates sensible defaults, provides reproducible profile artifacts for model owners, and exposes per-route unit-econ suggestions so engineers can make trade-offs with confidence. Design: 1) runtime: new `autotune` planner that ingests historical latency/throughput traces and suggests batch_size, max_latency_slo, and cache_prefix_policy; 2) quant_profiles: YAML templates for fp16/int8/q4_0/q4_1 tailored to decoder-only and encoder-decoder families with per-layer hints; 3) tooling: `redwood-uecon` CLI generates per-route token-cost forecasts and a Console widget that shows expected per-1M-token cost with and without recommended autotune changes; 4) rollout: feature-flagged on a per-customer basis and opt-in for Dedicated until monitored for two weeks. Implementation notes: Most changes are additive and behind runtime flags. The autotune planner lives under runtime/autotune/ and outputs JSON proposals to model-registry/profiles/. Quant templates are small YAMLs with defaults and explanatory comments. The UEcon tooling includes a lightweight simulator that extrapolates historical request distributions. Testing: unit tests for planner heuristics, integration smoke tests on canary cluster with synthetic traffic, e2e against eval datasets to ensure no quality regressions for int8 profiles (policy: require BLEU/ROUGE/LM-logprob thresholds depending on model type). Monitoring/metrics: new autotune.metrics.{proposal_count,applied_count,rollback_count,fails} and console graphs; SLO guards to auto-revert if p50 latency increases > 15%. Backwards compatibility: proposals are non-authoritative by default and require explicit apply via API or Console. Rollout plan: start with 5 beta customers on Dedicated, then widen to hosted customers with low traffic. Related: ENG-5872 linear spec, incident INT-992 follow-up fixes. Impact: early internal tests show median token cost reduction 18-24% for chat workloads and 5-10% latency improvement at p95 due to smarter batching. Caveats: quant profiles for very long-context LLMs are conservative; recommend manual review before wide apply.

diff_highlights: runtime/autotune/planner.py: new planner with core propose_batch_size() and propose_cache_policy() functions (300 LOC)
model-registry/profiles/*.yml: added 6 small templates (~120 LOC total) with comments and validation schema
cli/redwood-uecon/main.py: CLI to run simulation and print per-route recommendations (100 LOC)
console/widgets/uecon-cost-forecast.tsx: new widget that calls /api/v1/uecon/recommend and renders cost delta
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can we make the default KV cache TTL configurable per-customer? I think we should expose that in Console rather than bake it into the planner.
Asha Patel: Good call - added a per-customer override in deploy/feature-flags.yaml and console UI respects override. Planner falls back to global default.
Evan Zhou: Tests look good; question about quant profile validation: why do we allow per-layer overrides without an upper bound? Potential for OOM.
Asha Patel: Added validation to templates and a hard cap on per-layer int8 memory multiplier. Also added integration test that runs OOM-safety smoke tests on a small GPU in CI.
Priya Singh (approver): Verified metrics and rollout plan; OK to squash-merge once CI passes and docs updated.
CI Bot: autotune-ci passed on run #3 (flaky earlier due to docker pull).
notes_for_release: Feature flagged autotune defaults and UEcon tooling. Admins can opt-in via Console or API. Default behavior is opt-out for Hosted customers. See docs/autotune-quickstart.md for migration steps.
security_notes: No new secret storage. KMS/HSM integrations unchanged. Quant templates validated to avoid exposing model weights. CLI requires standard API token with uecon:read scope.
qa_summary: QA ran smoke against canary cluster; simulated traffic for chat, completion and embedding routes. No regressions in quality metrics. Observed expected cost reductions in synthetic runs. Two small follow-up fixes merged to address flaky CI and a UI tooltip.
how_to_test: Run CLI simulator: python -m cli.redwood-uecon.main --model gpt-j --trace sample_trace.json
Canary: enable feature flag for customer X and monitor autotune.metrics.* and p50/p95 latency graphs
